Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'rare' (potions.py:1205), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no counterpart -- the sim has no out-of-combat potion use at all; CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583) is the only entry point
Usage.issue: MECHANISM: PotionUsage.AnyTime means the game's Use button is live outside combat as well as in it, and PotionModel.OnUseWrapper is written for it -- `ICombatState combatState = Owner.Creature.CombatState` may legally be null and every later step null-checks it (PotionModel.cs:294, 298, 334, 336). The sim models no `usage` attribute and has exactly one use path, on CombatState: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, and the conformance layer treats UsePotion as a combat-only command in both the driver and the runner (conformance/combat_driver.py:16, conformance/runner.py:147-150). So the whole out-of-combat arm of this potion is unreachable in the sim: there is no action for it in the env and no replay path for it in the runner. LIVE, and it is one of the four AnyTime potions (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice) -- all four are ported, registered and reachable, so a recorded run that drinks one on the map, at a rest site or at a shop cannot be replayed; the UsePotion command falls to the _ROOM_BOUNDARY branch (conformance/runner.py:147-150) rather than being executed, so the belt and the HP the save asserts both drift. Filed as a gap, not a waiver: 'the sim has no path here' is today's content, not the shape of the divergence (binding rule 1).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:1207-1218)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

OnUse (protected override, EntropicBrew..issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The loop shape is right -- `while (Owner.HasOpenPotionSlots)` generate one potion and procure it, stopping when procurement fails (EntropicBrew.cs:21-28) vs `while player.has_open_potion_slot` at potions.py:1210-1218 -- and the parity generator is exactly right (G3). What is wrong is the procure VERB (G1: the sim goes through PlayerCombatState.add_potion, which runs neither Hook.ShouldProcurePotion nor Hook.AfterPotionProcured) and the legacy generator (G2: it filters out the three potions CanBeGeneratedInCombat excludes, where the source deliberately calls the OUT-of-combat factory here and does not).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the brew procures through PlayerCombatState.add_potion instead of PotionCmd.TryToProcure, dropping both of that verb's hooks
guards.issue: MECHANISM: EntropicBrew.cs:24 calls `PotionCmd.TryToProcure(potion, Owner)`, which opens with `if (!Hook.ShouldProcurePotion(...)) return NotAllowed;` and fires `await Hook.AfterPotionProcured(...)` on success (PotionCmd.cs:28-53). potions.py:1217 calls `player.add_potion(potion)`, whose own docstring states the omission (player.py:112-115: 'Combat-side procurement (Alchemize, Delicate Frond, Petrified Toad) does not run the Hook.ShouldProcurePotion gate today'). SAME MECHANISM as audit/records/relic/petrified_toad.json G1 and G2, both LIVE with executed witnesses, so this entry matches them per binding rule 3 and contributes a fourth trigger. What Entropic Brew adds is that it is the WORST trigger of the four: it procures up to three potions in one action, so a run holding Sozu (relics/sozu.py:26-27 returns False from should_procure_potion; granted by the ported Darv shrine) fills the whole belt in the sim where the game fills none, and a run holding Belt Buckle keeps 2 Dexterity it should have lost on the first potion. Both relics and this potion are ported and in their pools (potion_pools.py:48), and this is the only one of the 51 potions that procures.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the LEGACY generator is the wrong factory -- it applies the in-combat exclusion the source deliberately avoids here, and rolls uniformly instead of by rarity
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the source calls `PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat(Owner, RunState.Rng.CombatPotionGeneration)` (EntropicBrew.cs:23) -- the OUT-of-combat form, on purpose, even though the potion is usually drunk in a fight -- so Fairy in a Bottle, Fruit Juice and Regen Potion ARE reachable from Entropic Brew even though CreateRandomPotionInCombat would exclude them (PotionFactory.cs:31-34 vs :60-65). potions.py:1211-1216 forks on `rng_set is not None`: the parity arm calls potion_pools.generate_random_potion, which is the correct out-of-combat form (G3); the legacy arm calls potions.random_potion (potions.py:1262-1277), which filters `c.id not in NOT_GENERATED_IN_COMBAT` -- exactly the three potions that should still be reachable -- AND picks uniformly over the id-sorted implemented pool instead of rolling a rarity first. LIVE for the RL env, which never constructs an rng_set (full_env.py:788 and the CombatState default at combat.py:76): in training this potion can never produce a Fairy in a Bottle, and produces Rares at 1/48 each where the game produces the whole Rare bucket at 10%. The observation encoder reads the belt, so the divergence is observed. The parity path is unaffected, which is why this is grade B and not a stream desync.

guards.what: G3: the PARITY generator is right -- rarity roll then NextItem, on Rng.CombatPotionGeneration, over the unfiltered pool
guards.rationale: Verified against the factory rather than the docstring. PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotion is one `rng.NextFloat()` bucketed at <= 0.1 Rare / <= 0.35 Uncommon / else Common, then `rng.NextItem(list.Where(Rarity == rarity))` (PotionFactory.cs:67-81). potion_pools.roll_potion_rarity (potion_pools.py:118-126) and generate_random_potion (potion_pools.py:129-135) are that pair exactly, over POTION_POOL, and the sim reads `rng_set.combat_potion_generation` (potions.py:1214) -- the same named stream the C# passes. Two draws per potion on both sides, which is what keeps the stream counter aligned; a wrong stream here would be grade A (compare audit/records/relic/lost_coffer.json G2).

guards.what: N1: `HasOpenPotionSlots` is evaluated AFTER RemoveBeforeUse, so the brew refills its own slot
guards.rationale: PotionModel.OnUseWrapper calls RemoveBeforeUse at PotionModel.cs:293, before OnUse at :327, so by the time the loop runs the brew's own slot is null and the loop fills it. The sim does the same: CombatState.use_potion nulls the slot (combat.py:605) before calling potion.use (combat.py:609), and `player.has_open_potion_slot` is `None in self.potions` (player.py:146-149) against the same fixed-length list. Both sides therefore end with a full belt from a full belt. Executed shape check rather than assumption: the loop terminates on both sides because each successful procure fills exactly one null slot (Player.AddPotionInternal's `_potionSlots.IndexOf(null)` and player.py:116-118).

guards.what: N2: the belt is 3 slots in the sim and grows to 5 in the game, so this potion's yield differs whenever the growth relics are held
guards.issue: Recorded here because Entropic Brew is the potion whose OUTPUT is the belt size -- it fills every empty slot, so a wrong slot count is a wrong number of potions, not just a wrong capacity. The mechanism itself is already owned: audit/records/relic/potion_belt.json and audit/records/relic/alchemical_coffer.json, and PlayerCombatState.MAX_POTIONS = 3 (player.py:57) with RunState.add_potion_slots (run.py:492) as the growth path. This entry matches those verdicts per binding rule 3 and contributes the amplification: one Entropic Brew with Potion Belt held yields a different NUMBER of potions on the two sides, and each of those potions is a further CombatPotionGeneration draw pair -- so the divergence compounds into the RNG stream rather than staying a state difference.

guards.what: W: the shared PotionModel.OnUseWrapper pipeline every potion resolves through (audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md)
guards.issue: MECHANISM, shared by all 51 units and recorded once per record because PotionModel is one of harness.py's MODEL_ROOT_CLASSES, so no unit record enumerates it -- and unlike CardModel/PowerModel/RelicModel it is NOT covered by any seam record either, which is the coverage hole audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md exists to name. src/Core/Models/PotionModel.cs:291-342 in order: :293 RemoveBeforeUse (sim combat.py:603-606 nulls the slot and detaches the listener before the effect -- faithful); :297 Hook.BeforePotionUsed; :327 OnUse (this record's own hooks); :336 CombatManager.History.PotionUsed (no sim entry -- PotionUsedEntry.cs:9-38 adds only a Description string and an executed grep of src/ finds no game reader, so presentation only); :338 Hook.AfterPotionUsed (sim hooks.py:566-571 on_potion_used, dispatched at combat.py:610 -- faithful); :340 CheckForEmptyHand. TWO of those are LIVE gaps, and both are already owned by another record, so this entry MATCHES their verdicts per binding rule 3 rather than re-deriving them. (1) BeforePotionUsed has no sim dispatcher at all -- hooks.py declares only on_potion_used, whose own docstring says it mirrors AfterPotionUsed -- and its single C# implementer SurroundedPower.cs:82 is ported at powers.py:2523, so throwing a potion at the far Kaiser Crab arm does not turn the player to face it: audit/records/power/surrounded.json, gap, live. (2) CombatManager.cs:887-893 CheckForEmptyHand has exactly two callers, CardModel.cs:1992 and PotionModel.cs:340, and the sim's only on_hand_emptied call site is player.py:197 -- the end-of-turn flush CombatManager.cs:880-883 explicitly excludes: audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G1, gap, LIVE, executed with a potion witness. Reachable from EVERY potion, not only the hand-emptying ones, because C# tests the hand AFTER the use. Rollup `gap` per binding rule 4.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
